title: The Tea Horse Road
summary: The Tea Horse Road was a network of mountain trade routes on which tea travelled from Sichuan and Yunnan to Tibet in exchange for horses. Pages date its history from the early Tang dynasty into the Qing, and one traces porters carrying tea from Ya'an through Kangding to Lhasa.

uncertainty.note: China Daily says the road's history runs from the early Tang to the late Qing and the Republic era; National Geographic gives no founding date, notes tea reached Tibet by legend with a Tang princess's marriage in A.D. 641, an agency set up in 1074, and porter work ending after 1949. The record id uses 700 as a rough early-Tang placeholder, not a sourced date. The Sichuan stops are undated.

importance.justification: A long-lived mountain trade route that moved tea to Tibet and horses to China and linked Sichuan and Yunnan with Lhasa.

sources.title: Legacy of Tea Horse Road lives on in Yunnan village
sources.author: Li You

beats.caption: Tea is carried from Ya'an by porters to Kangding, where it is packed in yak-skin cases for the long trek to Lhasa.
The route runs on across the Tibetan Plateau to Lhasa, whose Drepung Monastery lies at the road's western end.
By the 11th century brick tea served as currency, and a Sichuan Tea and Horse Agency was set up in 1074.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the dating. No opened page gives a founding year; the id's 700 is a placeholder, and the start of 618 is the Tang dynasty's own start year, not a sourced founding. Only one branch (Sichuan-Tibet) is plotted; China Daily's Pu'er/Yunnan branch is not. The 1074 and 11th-century currency claims come from National Geographic only.
